newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Rite Aid to buy Thrifty Payless.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Rite Aid to buy Thrifty Payless.

text.p: Rite Aid Corp announced Monday that it would buy Thrifty Payless Holdings for about 38.7 million shares of Rite Aid common stock, representing a 31.2 percent interest in the combined entity.
Based on Rite Aid's Friday stock close of 35-7/8, the deal is worth about $1.39 billion.
The following is a full text of Rite Aid's press release:

CAMP HILL, PA and WILSONVILLE, OR,--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 14, 1996-- Rite Aid Corporation today announced that it has entered into a definitive merger agreement to acquire Thrifty PayLess, Inc, the largest drugstore chain in the western United States.

This merger creates a drugstore chain of more than 3,500 drugstores with revenues of approximately $10 billion in 26 states and the District of Columbia. Rite Aid said that the transaction is expected to be accretive to earnings in 1997. Under the terms of the agreement each share of Thrifty PayLess will be converted into 0.65 shares of Rite Aid.

Rite Aid also announced it has entered into a definitive agreement to sell approximately 200 drugstores located in North and South Carolina to Thrift Drug, Inc., a division of J.C. Penney Company. Rite Aid also anticipates exiting Florida, Georgia and Alabama.

Martin Grass, Chairman and CEO of Rite Aid said, "These transactions are part of a strategic realignment intended to assure growth in areas where we will have a leading position. After the acquisition, Rite Aid will operate in 25 of the top 50 metropolitan statistical areas in the United States, in 21 of which it will hold the number one or number two position. Thrifty PayLess currently holds the number one or number two position in drugstore sales in 90 percent of the metropolitan areas in which it operates."

Mr. Grass added, "The acquisition of the West Coast's largest drugstore chain enables us to extend our geographic reach and provide more opportunities in higher growth areas. We expect that the acquisition will result in cost savings of at least $65 million during the first full year of operation from elimination of duplicative overhead and by more efficient purchasing. This will result in more competitive pharmacy pricing to the consumer."

Rite Aid intends to close the Thrifty PayLess corporate offices in Wilsonville, Oregon, and to transfer all of its functions to Rite Aid headquarters in Camp Hill, Pennsylvania. As has been Rite Aid's custom in prior acquisitions, it will provide excellent severance packages and out-placement counseling to all affected headquarters personnel.

Mr. Grass continued, "Combining Thrifty PayLess with Rite Aid's strong cost control culture will reduce selling, general, and administrative expenses, and result in significant operational efficiencies. Rite Aid's more sophisticated technology will provide significant benefits to Thrifty PayLess stores and its customers. Rite Aid's satellite-linked pharmacy systems will enhance the prescription business. In addition, its state-of-the-art point of sale front end automatic replenishment program will improve Thrifty PayLess' merchandising and in-stock conditions.

Thrifty PayLess operates, entirely separate from its drugstore chain, Bi-Mart, a membership discount stores company. Bi-Mart, consisting of 44 stores, has annual sales of $365 million. Rite Aid intends to divest this business as soon as practical after completing the acquisition.

The transaction is subject to customary conditions, including approval by both companies' shareholders and regulatory agencies. The exchange ratio for the merger is fixed. However, Thrifty PayLess will not be obligated to close unless after the fulfillment of all other customary closing conditions, and prior to May 1, 1997, the average closing sales price of Rite Aid common stock per share as reported on the NYSE composite tape for the five trading days immediately preceding the closing date (the "Five Day Measuring Period") shall be at least $30.75, provided however that this condition shall be deemed satisfied if such average closing sales price is, though less than $30.75, more than $29 so long as such average closing sales price does not represent a diminution below $36.375 which, expressed as a percentage, exceeds the diminution (if any), also expressed as a percentage, of the average reported closing Dow Jones Industrial Average during the Five Day Measuring Period below 5,934.

In the event of a termination due to a competing takeover proposal or certain other circumstances, Thrifty PayLess would be obligated to pay Rite Aid a termination fee of $37.5 million, and Rite Aid would be entitled to $5 million in out-of-pocket expenses. Rite Aid would be obligated to pay similar amounts to Thrifty PayLess if Rite Aid's shareholders should reject the transaction. The transaction is expected to close in early 1997.

In connection with the Thrifty PayLess acquisition, Rite Aid expects to establish a $125 million reserve for restructuring and integration costs which will be recorded in conjunction with the closing of the acquisition.

Under the terms of the merger agreement, Thrifty PayLess shareholders will receive an aggregate of approximately 38.7 million shares of Rite Aid common stock, representing a 31.2 percent interest in the combined entity. Green Equity Investors, L.P. and Kmart Corporation, who together own about 43 percent of Thrifty PayLess outstanding common stock, have agreed to vote in favor of the merger and against any other transaction. Green Equity Investors, L.P. and Kmart will hold a 7.6 percent and a 6.0 percent interest in Rite Aid Corporation, respectively.
Rite Aid is the largest operator of retail drugstores in the United States, with 2,809 stores in 22 eastern states and the District of Columbia, and revenues of approximately $5.9 billion.

Thrifty PayLess is the largest drugstore chain in the western United States, with 1,007 drugstores in ten states, with drugstore revenues of $4.4 billion. Thrifty PayLess was formed under the sponsorship of Leonard Green & Partners in 1994 with the combination of Thrifty, founded in 1929, and PayLess, founded in 1939. Thrifty PayLess became publicly owned in April, 1996.

Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp. acted as merger advisor and provided a fairness opinion to Rite Aid Corp. Goldman, Sachs & Co. acted as merger advisor and provided a fairness opinion to Thrifty PayLess, Inc.
